text:
Jacob Trouba is in San Jose now, his fourth NHL team after Winnipeg, the Rangers and Anaheim, and he's doing what he's always done: playing a lot. His 22:07 a night is a big load for a 32-year-old on a team still finding itself, and he has 2 goals and 11 points in 25 games.

The numbers are honest about his game. He sits right in the middle of our talent range for scoring, the Sharks win 46.1% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with him, a couple of points better than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows the two sides: he stops 16% of entries at his blue line (typical is 11%), but only 28% of his exits keep the puck.

He shoots a lot (41 shots), though often from the outside. He's a former Messier Leadership Award winner, and after a loss to Calgary on Nov. 17, Sportsnaut's headline read: Trouba on Missing Sherwood, “Not Our Best Game”. On a young team, the minutes and the voice are the point.
headline: Trouba is still eating minutes
